# Climat (climat.today), by Chainflux

> Climat is an origination workspace for carbon project developers. It checks methodology applicability, reports what evidence is missing, and drafts the project document from your evidence with a citation on every claim. Built by Chainflux in Bengaluru, India. Climat is not a registry and not a validation body.

Every page on this site has a Markdown version at the same address with `index.md` appended. Educational pages cite the primary registry documents they rest on and carry the date they were last checked. The full text of the site is in [llms-full.txt](https://climat.today/llms-full.txt).

## Product

- [How Climat works: from methodology choice to export](https://climat.today/product/index.md): A step-by-step walkthrough of Climat: intake built from the methodology, applicability check, evidence gap report, cited drafting, human review and export.
- [Applicability check](https://climat.today/product/applicability-check/index.md): The applicability check evaluates every applicability condition of the chosen methodology against the project's intake and returns one of three results for each: pass, fail, or needs review. It is rule-based, not generated, and a condition that calls for judgment is sent to a person instead of being guessed.
- [Document drafting](https://climat.today/product/document-drafting/index.md): Climat drafts each section of the registry's project document from the project's own intake and uploaded evidence. Every statement cites its origin: the intake, an excerpt of the evidence, or the methodology. Citations to uploads are checked against the text supplied, conflicts are raised as warnings, and a person finalizes every section.
- [Pre-validation review](https://climat.today/product/pre-validation/index.md): Pre-validation is a critical review of a project document carried out before it is submitted to a validation and verification body, so that likely findings are fixed first. Climat's pre-validation review is in development: it is built and tested in the engine, and is not yet available to users.
- [Monitoring periods](https://climat.today/product/monitoring/index.md): After a project is registered, it has to collect the data its methodology requires and report it for each monitoring period. Climat's monitoring tracking is in development: it is built and tested in the engine, and is not yet available to users.

## Methodologies

- [Methodologies](https://climat.today/methodologies/index.md): A methodology is the rulebook a carbon project is assessed against. For each methodology Climat supports, these pages explain what it covers, which conditions a project must meet, how additionality and the baseline are established, and what has to be monitored. Every page names the version it describes and the date it was checked.
- [VM0047 explained: applicability, additionality, baseline and monitoring](https://climat.today/methodologies/vm0047/index.md): VM0047 is Verra's methodology for afforestation, reforestation and revegetation. Version 1.1, active since 14 May 2025, credits carbon dioxide removals under two mutually exclusive approaches: an area-based approach that uses a remote-sensing performance benchmark, and a census-based approach for dispersed planting of up to 50 planting units per hectare with a zero baseline.
- [VMR0017 explained: eligibility, additionality, baseline and monitoring](https://climat.today/methodologies/vmr0017/index.md): VMR0017 Grid-Connected Electricity Generation from Renewable Sources (ACM0002 Revision) is a Verra methodology revision, version 1.0 of 23 April 2026. It cannot be used on its own: the procedures of CDM methodology ACM0002, v22.0, apply except where VMR0017 replaces them. It sets eligibility through a technology, capacity and geography table, replaces four CDM tools with VCS tools, adds project emissions from battery fire suppression agents, and treats the plant's embodied emissions as leakage.

## Registries

- [Registries](https://climat.today/registries/index.md): Each carbon standard requires its own project document, with its own sections in its own order. These pages set out what the Verra Verified Carbon Standard and the Gold Standard for the Global Goals each ask a project developer to write, and the program rules that shape a project's timeline.
- [The Gold Standard PDD: every section and what it must establish](https://climat.today/registries/gold-standard/index.md): A Gold Standard for the Global Goals project is documented in the Project Design Document template v2.0 of 15 May 2026: key project information, a project impact summary, and sections A to I. The PDD must show methodology compliance, a safeguarding assessment, a stakeholder consultation, and monitored contributions to at least three Sustainable Development Goals, including SDG 13.
- [The Verra VCS project description: every section and what it must establish](https://climat.today/registries/verra-vcs/index.md): The Verra VCS project description is written on VCS Project Description Template v5.0A or v5.0B, both issued 9 June 2026. Each has five numbered sections (project details, safeguards and stakeholder engagement, application of methodology, quantification, monitoring) and two standing appendices. A project start date before 1 January 2027 means v5.0A; on or after that date, v5.0B.

## Guides

- [Guides](https://climat.today/guides/index.md): Practical guides for people who prepare carbon projects for registration. Each guide answers one question, cites the registry documents it rests on, names the version of each standard it describes, and carries the date it was last checked.
- [What is additionality in a carbon project?](https://climat.today/guides/additionality/index.md): Additionality means a carbon project's emission reductions or removals exceed business as usual and the activity would not have happened without carbon revenue. The applied methodology sets the test: regulatory surplus plus investment analysis or barrier analysis and common practice analysis, or a performance benchmark or positive list. Verra's current tool is VT0008 Additionality Assessment, v1.0.
- [Applicability conditions: how to tell whether a methodology fits](https://climat.today/guides/applicability-conditions/index.md): Applicability conditions are the criteria in a carbon methodology that decide which project activities may use it, such as geography, technology, scale, dates and land-use history. A project must meet every condition, including those in referenced tools and modules, and justify each one separately in the project document. Validators test each condition against evidence.
- [How to register a carbon project](https://climat.today/guides/how-to-register-a-carbon-project/index.md): Registering a carbon project follows one sequence under Verra VCS and Gold Standard: select a methodology, list the project, consult stakeholders, pass validation by an approved validation/verification body, and pass the registry's review. Credits are issued later, after monitoring and verification. Verra calls the approval registration; Gold Standard calls it design certification.
- [Validation vs verification in carbon projects](https://climat.today/guides/validation-and-verification/index.md): Validation is the independent assessment of a carbon project's design before registration. Verification is the periodic, after-the-fact assessment of the emission reductions or removals the project reports. A validation/verification body approved by the registry performs both, raises findings that the developer must close, and issues a report and opinion that the registry then reviews.
- [Verra vs Gold Standard for project developers](https://climat.today/guides/verra-vs-gold-standard/index.md): Verra's Verified Carbon Standard (VCS) covers all seven Kyoto Protocol gases and project types such as avoided deforestation and geological carbon storage. Gold Standard for the Global Goals credits only carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide, requires two rounds of stakeholder consultation, and certifies projects in five-year cycles. Deadlines, buffers, labels and fees also differ.
- [What is a project design document (PDD)?](https://climat.today/guides/what-is-a-pdd/index.md): A project design document (PDD) describes a carbon project and demonstrates that it meets the rules of a carbon standard and the applied methodology. The developer writes it, a validation/verification body audits it, and the registry publishes it. Verra calls it a project description; Gold Standard, the CDM and the Article 6.4 mechanism call it a PDD.

## Reference

- [Glossary of carbon project terms](https://climat.today/glossary/index.md): Short definitions of the terms that appear in carbon project documents and in the standards that govern them. Each definition names the document it rests on. Where standards use a term differently, the definition says so.

## Company

- [About Climat](https://climat.today/about/index.md): Climat is an origination workspace for carbon project developers, built by Chainflux in Bengaluru, India. It exists because preparing a project document is slow and expensive, and much of that cost comes from problems that could have been found before validation began.
- [Contact us](https://climat.today/contact/index.md): Climat is in early access. Tell us which methodology you are working under and where the project stands, and we will arrange a working session on a real project.
- [How we use AI](https://climat.today/trust/index.md): Climat uses a language model to draft sections of the project document and to compare the intake with the uploaded evidence. The applicability check and the evidence gap report are rule-based and are not generated. Citations are checked, a person finalizes every section, and the use of AI is disclosed to the validation body.
